title: Currying preserves finite product measures
statement: Let $I,J$ be finite sets, and let $B$ be a measurable space with measurable singletons. For each $i\in I$ and $j\in J$, let $\mu_{ij}$ be a sigma-finite measure on $B$. The currying bijection from arrays indexed by $I\times J$ to $I$-indexed arrays of $J$-indexed arrays sends the product measure with coordinate measures $\mu_{ij}$ to the iterated product measure that first groups coordinates by $i$ and then by $j$.
replaced: Let $I,J,B$ be finite sets, let $B$ carry a measurable structure with measurable singletons, and let $\mu_{ij}$ be sigma-finite measures on $B$. The bijection $B^{I\times J}\to(B^J)^I$ sending $x$ to the array $i\mapsto(j\mapsto x(i,j))$ pushes $\bigotimes_{(i,j)}\mu_{ij}$ to $\bigotimes_i\bigotimes_j\mu_{ij}$.
